history.0.1: first declaration, from the orchestrator update order
history.0.2: PT-4a falsified 0.1 on tomato season 0: a heat or cold wave also changes outdoor_relative_humidity_pct (the twin recomputes the outdoor humidity from the shifted temperature), an edge outdoor_temperature_c -> outdoor_relative_humidity_pct that 0.1 had not declared. Added; the test of 0.2 must use other episodes.
history.0.3: nutrient line, level 0b: the series of the reduced nutrient model (nutrient_applied, available, extracted, leached, status) and the entry point of the FERTILIZATION event, written from nutrient_balance.py and the update order of step_at BEFORE any check; edges read from the code except those marked with a question mark. The same-step cycle between the pool and the leaching is avoided by declaring the leaching as a function of the pool of the previous step, the dose and the uptake.
history.0.4: nutrient line, level 1 (optional NITROGEN_DEMAND model), written from nitrogen_demand.py and the orchestrator BEFORE the check: the crop nitrogen and the critical nitrogen, the edges of the uptake and the status to them, and the drainage as a parent of the leaching (the leaching fraction is set by the drainage of the same step). The edges are a union for both nutrient models: those that exist only in one model are ignored where the series is absent.

status: PROVISIONAL declaration written from the update order of CropDigitalTwinOrchestrator.step_at (weather, greenhouse microclimate, crop environment, phenology, radiation, water, nutrients, climate stress, combined factor, actual growth) and from the controller's contract (stateless, decides at the start of step n from the state of step n-1). Written BEFORE the intervention check of PT-4a; edges marked '?' are assumptions not read from the code. The graph is a hypothesis about the twin, tested by re-simulation, not a fact about real greenhouses.
notation: child: [parent, ...]; 'parent' is a same-step (lag 0) edge, 'parent@1' an edge from the previous step's value; a trailing '?' marks an assumed edge. Variables not listed are exogenous or not covered.
